title: FLASHBACK TABLE same-name parent identity drift leaves recovered orphan rows

payload.p_check: historical child and parent were valid together before drop
payload.q_claim: recovered child rows remain valid against the current referenced object
payload.fault: drop historical parent, recreate an empty or incompatible table under the same name, then FLASHBACK TABLE the child
payload.oracle: existing-row LEFT JOIN differential plus future Foreign_Key_Check plan and ADMIN CHECK TABLE
controls: same-name parent with original row GREEN

name: Recovered FK rows must be valid against the current referenced object

payload.p_check: historical child and parent were valid together before drop
payload.q_claim: recovered child rows remain valid against the current referenced object
payload.missing_dimension: current parent row membership and object identity

name: Recovered child rowset matches current parent rowset

payload.tier1: LEFT JOIN recovered child rows to current parent and count missing keys
payload.tier2: EXPLAIN future invalid INSERT and ADMIN CHECK TABLE
payload.red: existing orphan row with recovery success
payload.green: rowset consistent with parent and invalid future insert rejected

lessons.root_accounting: independent from id30016 because parent existence passes and existing-row membership is the missing proof
lessons.method: reuse the old FK oracle and mutate only current parent identity/rowset

environment.shape: historical child FK with ON DELETE CASCADE and same-name parent replacement

observed: recovered c row (10,1) joins same-name replacement p(id=1)
DELETE FROM p WHERE id=1 succeeds
child row count changes from 1 to 0 through ON DELETE CASCADE
SHOW CREATE TABLE c still declares fk_c_p REFERENCES p(id) ON DELETE CASCADE

lessons.consequence_escalation: same root as existing-row identity drift, but a downstream cascade action demonstrates direct user-visible data loss
lessons.method: after proving a rebound reference, execute the reference owner's destructive action and check the recovered object's rowset
